operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers everywhere: People_ID, Company_ID, Year_working, Sales_in_Billion; must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
FK in employment uses backtick-quoted parent `company`("Company_ID") and `people`("People_ID") — DDL text has backticks; sqlite_master DDL must be replayed verbatim.

company.Company_ID declared REAL, storage class real, values 1.0..19.0; employment.Company_ID declared INT, storage integer, values 7,11,13,15,17 — FK child/parent storage classes differ (int vs real).
employment.Company_ID values (7,11,13,15,17) are a subset of company.Company_ID (1..19) but not contiguous; FK join is int=real comparison.
Composite PK on employment (Company_ID, People_ID); both members are also FK children — PK-duplicate drop and FK fill interact.
All columns notnull=0 (nullable) despite being PK members; upstream does not enforce NOT NULL, so NULL PK rows can be inserted and then dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
Tiny tables: people=7, company=19, employment=5 rows. choose_table_sizes will produce sizes far larger than originals (30..2500), so FK parent pools are small relative to child demand.
No unique/check constraints in DDL; no indexes, views, triggers.
people.Nationality has a typo value 'United Kindom' (distinct=2) — literal pool will carry the typo.
company.Name and people.Name share column name 'Name' across tables; literal pool anchors by column name will cross-contaminate unless table qualifier present.
employment.Year_working is a year-like INT but declared INT (not YEAR) — dispatches to Number, not the year fuzzer.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no missing parents.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer for all INT/REAL columns: scale from type args (none -> default), range [-10^scale, 10^scale]; Company_ID REAL and People_ID INT both get fresh random ints/floats, so PKs are random large numbers, not 1..N.

String fuzzer for Name/Nationality/Graduation_College/Headquarters/Industry: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20, plus 5 sampled originals, plus contamination — implausible company/person names drive FN on name-equality queries.

FK fill: employment.Company_ID draws from company.Company_ID final values (real floats), employment.People_ID from people.People_ID (ints) — type mismatch int vs real may still join in sqlite but comparisons like = may miss.
Composite PK (Company_ID, People_ID) on employment: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate pairs; with small parent pools and large n, many rows dropped, shrinking employment.

Single-column PKs (people.People_ID, company.Company_ID) get max_l0=inf so fresh draws never reused — PKs are near-unique random numbers, so joins on PK rarely match literal-pool values from train SQL.
Literal pool from train SQL: values like 'USA', 'Oil and gas', 'Banking' get appended to Headquarters/Industry anchors; Number columns get numeric literals from queries.
p=0.2 default, 0.3 chance whole instance p=0 — with p=0, Number/String always fresh, no original reuse, more implausible values.
No Date/Time/Bool columns, so date/time fuzzers unused; no crash-fallback types.
Known FN driver: random strings for Name/Headquarters/Industry make WHERE Name='ExxonMobil' return empty in generated DBs.
Known FP driver: small parent pools + large child sizes create many-to-one FK fan-out not present in original (original employment has 5 rows, distinct Company_ID=5).
Year_working as Number: random ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale default), so year comparisons like Year_working>3 mostly true — implausible.
